note: Topology-aware peel (peel_topo_aware.py MVP) vs route-after-SABRE. Correct + fully topology-valid (0 illegal edges, no SABRE) but NOT competitive on 2q count. Routing (naive per-row SWAP) is the loss; reductions-only is comparable to route-after.
setting: square topology, perfect Hamiltonian path, post_transpile(all2all=False) cleanup
diagnosis: UCCSD doubles have disconnected 2-block support; 51-76% rows connected even with perfect layout; no static layout connects all doubles. Naive per-row SWAP routing >> SABRE. reductions-only ~18k comparable to route-after 25k.
verdict: naive co-design verified working but not impressive; beating route-after needs Steiner CNOT fan-in + fSWAP fusion + cross-row-sharing preservation (multi-week, MPLS/2QAN-level).
